proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\kappa\ge0\).  For a one-period total nonprice utility vector \(z\), the utility index and choice-maximization assumptions determine the first-period winner and, for each possible lag \(a\in M_1\), the second-period winner.  Outside the finite union of pairwise utility-tie hyperplanes this produces a unique response table \(f(z)\).  Conditional on \(\lambda\), the vector \(z=\lambda+\epsilon_t\) is Lebesgue absolutely continuous, so every such hyperplane has probability zero.  Moreover, the realized \(z\) satisfies all strict comparisons defining \(f(z)\), and therefore \(f(z)\in F_\kappa\) by \(\texttt{lem:strict-cycle-feasibility}\).

For almost every \(\lambda\), define
\[
 q_f(\lambda)
 =\Pr\{f(\lambda+\epsilon_t)=f\mid\lambda\},
 \qquad f\in F_\kappa.
\]
The conditional-homogeneity assumption makes this definition independent of \(t\), and the no-tie conclusion gives \(q(\lambda)\in\Delta(F_\kappa)\).  Conditional independence, together with the fact that the second-period response after the realized first choice \(a\) is \(f_2(a)\), gives for every \(a\in M_1\) and \(b\in M_2\)
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr(Y_1=a,Y_2=b\mid\lambda)
 &=\Pr\{f_1(\lambda+\epsilon_1)=a\mid\lambda\}
   \Pr\{f_2(a;\lambda+\epsilon_2)=b\mid\lambda\}\\
 &=r_a(q(\lambda))s_{ab}(q(\lambda))
 =v_{ab}(q(\lambda)).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
 P=\int v(q(\lambda))\,dF_\lambda(\lambda).
\]
The set \(\Delta(F_\kappa)\) is compact and \(v\) is continuous, so its image is compact.  Every point of that image belongs to the affine hyperplane \(\{x\in\mathbb R^m:\sum_jx_j=1\}\), of dimension \(m-1\).  If a convex combination uses more than \(m\) image points, affine dependence permits the same weight-elimination argument used in \(\texttt{lem:observable-moment-compression}\), repeated until at most \(m\) points remain.  Hence its convex hull is the continuous image of the compact set of at most \(m\) image points and mixing weights, and is therefore compact.  Finite simple-function approximations to the displayed integral lie in this convex hull and converge to \(P\); closedness therefore yields
\[
 P\in\operatorname{conv}\{v(q):q\in\Delta(F_\kappa)\}=\mathcal C_\kappa.
\]
This proves necessity.  Its load-bearing probabilistic premise is precisely the fixed-cell conditional factorization supplied by conditional independence and conditional homogeneity; absolute continuity is used here to remove ties.

Conversely, take \(P\in\mathcal C_\kappa\).  The same affine-dependence elimination gives
\[
 P=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L_0}\omega_\ell v(q^\ell),
 \qquad
 1\le L_0\le m,
 \qquad
 \omega_\ell\ge0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{\ell=1}^{L_0}\omega_\ell=1.
\]
For every \(\ell\) and every \(f\) with \(q_f^\ell>0\), \(\texttt{lem:strict-cycle-feasibility}\) supplies an open axis-aligned cube \(B_{\ell f}\) contained in the strict response patch of \(f\).  Let \(G_\ell\) assign mass \(q_f^\ell\) uniformly on \(B_{\ell f}\).  This is an absolutely continuous probability law and its response-table probabilities are exactly \(q^\ell\).  Choose distinct real constants \(c_\ell\), set
\[
 \lambda^\ell=(c_\ell,\ldots,c_\ell)\in\mathbb R^J,
\]
and assign mass \(\omega_\ell\) to \(\lambda=\lambda^\ell\).  Given \(\lambda^\ell\), draw \(Z_1,Z_2\) independently with common law \(G_\ell\), and put \(\epsilon_t=Z_t-\lambda^\ell\).  Then \(\epsilon_1\) and \(\epsilon_2\) are conditionally iid and absolutely continuous, while \(\lambda^\ell+\epsilon_t=Z_t\).  The conditional path law is therefore \(v(q^\ell)\), and mixing over \(\ell\) produces exactly \(P\).  All supported draws lie in strict patches, so maximizers are unique.  Zero path probabilities and boundary points require no limiting argument.  This establishes exact sufficiency using at most \(m\) fixed-effect types.

The two directions delimit the class claim.  The necessity argument uses the stated fixed-cell sequential-exogeneity and stationarity factorization plus no ties, whereas the reverse direction constructs conditionally iid, absolutely continuous shocks.  Thus the equality is established for the maintained fixed-cell class with the explicit no-tie and absolute-continuity regularity, not for an unspecified larger published class.

There are finitely many response tables, and each finite comparison multigraph has finitely many directed simple cycles.  From \(\texttt{def:comparison-graph}\), every cycle weight has the form
\[
 W_C(\kappa)=A_C+B_C\kappa,
\]
where rational prices imply \(A_C\in\mathbb Q\), and the switching indicators imply \(B_C\in\mathbb Z\).  Each nonconstant weight has at most one root.  Thus adjoining zero to all nonnegative roots produces a finite set \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\), and its maximum \(K\) is finite and rational.

Fix \(\kappa>K\).  If \(B_C>0\), then \(W_C(\kappa)>0\): this holds to the right of its nonnegative root, while a negative root implies \(A_C>0\) and positivity on the entire nonnegative half-line.  If \(B_C<0\), the analogous sign analysis gives \(W_C(\kappa)<0\).  If \(B_C=0\), strict positivity is equivalent to \(A_C>0\).  Therefore, by \(\texttt{lem:strict-cycle-feasibility}\) and \(\texttt{def:terminal-body}\),
\[
 F_\kappa=F_\infty\qquad(\kappa>K),
\]
and the definitions of the two compatible bodies give
\[
 \mathcal C_\kappa=\mathcal C_\infty\qquad(\kappa>K).
\]

Assume \(\Theta(P)\ne\varnothing\).  If \(P\in\mathcal C_\infty\), terminal equality implies \((K,+\infty)\subseteq\Theta(P)\), so \(U(P)=+\infty\).  If \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\), no \(\kappa>K\) is compatible; the nonempty set \(\Theta(P)\) is then bounded above, and \(U(P)<+\infty\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal C_\infty\), supplied by \(\texttt{thm:sharp-iid-body}\) and terminal equality, implies that the continuous function \(Q\mapsto\|P-Q\|_\infty\) attains its minimum.  Hence
\[
 P\notin\mathcal C_\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal C_\infty}\|P-Q\|_\infty>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 D_\infty(P)>0.
\]

Suppose \(P\in\mathcal C_{\kappa_0}\).  Choose a finite convex representation of \(P\) and collect the finitely many response tables having positive mass in it.  Every simple-cycle weight for each collected table is strictly positive at \(\kappa_0\).  Continuity of these finitely many affine weights gives a relative neighborhood \(N\) of \(\kappa_0\) in \([0,+\infty)\) on which all remain positive.  The same probability vectors and outer mixing weights then witness \(P\in\mathcal C_\kappa\) for every \(\kappa\in N\).  Thus \(\Theta(P)\) is relatively open.

Removing the finite set \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) partitions \([0,+\infty)\) into finitely many open price strata.  On each stratum every affine cycle weight has constant sign, so \(F_\kappa\) and \(\mathcal C_\kappa\) are constant.  Testing the finitely many strata and breakpoint values therefore represents \(\Theta(P)\) as a finite union of relatively open intervals.  Any finite upper endpoint must be a stratum boundary, hence belongs to \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\), and relative openness implies that the endpoint is not attained.

For a fixed response set \(F\), membership has the explicit finite existential form
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 w_\ell\ge0,\qquad \sum_{\ell=1}^{m}w_\ell=1,
 \qquad
 q_{\ell f}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}=1,\\
 P_{ab}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}w_\ell
 \left(\sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}\mathbf 1\{f_1=a\}\right)
 \left(\sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}\mathbf 1\{f_2(a)=b\}\right)
 \quad(a\in M_1,b\in M_2).
 \end{gathered}
\]
The \(m\)-component bound follows from \(\texttt{thm:sharp-iid-body}\).  For arbitrary real coordinates of \(P\), this display is a finite semialgebraic characterization with \(P\) as a real parameter; its coefficients are not claimed to be rational.  An exact-real oracle that decides each displayed existential formula, applied to one representative of every open stratum and separately to every breakpoint response set, recovers \(\Theta(P)\) and its exact upper endpoint.  If \(P\) is rational, all coefficients are rational.  If each coordinate of \(P\) is instead a represented real-algebraic number, adjoining its integer defining polynomial and rational isolating interval reduces exact signs to the certified real-algebraic procedure in \(\texttt{lem:represented-algebraic-semialgebraic-decision}\).  Thus rational root isolation and sign decomposition give an unconditional implementation only for these represented inputs.  An arbitrary unrepresented real table receives the oracle-relative characterization, not a false rational-coefficient algorithmic guarantee.  No step uses monotonicity in \(\kappa\).

Finally, the class implication is asymmetric.  If \(P\in\mathcal C_\infty\), the constructive sufficiency part of \(\texttt{thm:sharp-iid-body}\) rationalizes \(P\) at every \(\kappa>K\) within the maintained absolutely continuous conditional-iid subclass.  Nonidentification therefore transfers to every larger class containing that subclass.  In contrast, \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\) excludes only laws for which the theorem's necessity factorization applies; subclass exclusion alone cannot exclude a rationalization available in a larger class.

Fix \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\) and write \(N=|H|\).  The set \(F_\kappa\) is nonempty because a \(z\) outside the finite union of tie hyperplanes induces a strict response table.  The terminal equality in \(\texttt{thm:terminal-frontier}\), evaluated at any \(\kappa>K\), then shows that \(F_\infty\) is nonempty.  If \(N=1\), its simplex and every rational grid contain the same single point, so \(\mathcal C_{H,L}=\mathcal C_H\) and \(e_{H,L}=0\).

Suppose \(N\ge2\) and take \(q\in\Delta(H)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:observable-moment-compression}\), there is \(\bar q\in\Delta(H)\) with
\[
 v(\bar q)=v(q),
 \qquad
 k:=|\operatorname{supp}(\bar q)|
 \le\min\{N,m\}.
\]
Order its supported tables as \(f_1,\ldots,f_k\).  For \(j<k\), put
\[
 q'_{f_j}=\frac{\lfloor L\bar q_{f_j}\rfloor}{L},
 \qquad
 q'_{f_k}=1-\sum_{j<k}q'_{f_j},
\]
and set all remaining coordinates to zero.  Then \(q'\in\mathcal G_{H,L}\), and
\[
 \|\bar q-q'\|_1
 =2\sum_{j<k}\left(\bar q_{f_j}-q'_{f_j}\right)
 \le\frac{2(k-1)}{L}
 \le\frac{2(\min\{N,m\}-1)}{L}.
\]
For any subset \(E\subseteq H\),
\[
 |\bar q(E)-q'(E)|
 \le\frac12\|\bar q-q'\|_1.
\]
Every \(r_a\) and \(s_{ab}\) is the probability of such a subset.  With \(\Delta_q=\|\bar q-q'\|_1\) and using that all factors lie in \([0,1]\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |v_{ab}(q)-v_{ab}(q')|
 &=|r_a(\bar q)s_{ab}(\bar q)-r_a(q')s_{ab}(q')|\\
 &\le |r_a(\bar q)-r_a(q')|s_{ab}(\bar q)
      +r_a(q')|s_{ab}(\bar q)-s_{ab}(q')|\\
 &\le\Delta_q.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The left side is also at most one.  Therefore
\[
 \|v(q)-v(q')\|_\infty
 \le e_{H,L}
 =\min\left\{1,\frac{2(\min\{N,m\}-1)}{L}\right\}.
\]

The grid image is contained in the full image, so \(\mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H\).  Conversely, write any \(Q\in\mathcal C_H\) as
\[
 Q=\sum_{j=1}^{s}\theta_jv(q^j),
 \qquad \theta_j\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_j\theta_j=1.
\]
Applying the preceding compression and rounding separately to every \(q^j\) gives \(q^{j\prime}\in\mathcal G_{H,L}\).  Thus
\[
 Q_L=\sum_{j=1}^{s}\theta_jv(q^{j\prime})\in\mathcal C_{H,L},
 \qquad
 \|Q-Q_L\|_\infty
 \le\sum_j\theta_j\|v(q^j)-v(q^{j\prime})\|_\infty
 \le e_{H,L}.
\]
This proves
\[
 \mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H
 \subseteq\mathcal C_{H,L}+[-e_{H,L},e_{H,L}]^m.
\]

Both sets are compact.  The first inclusion gives
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)\le d_{H,L}(R).
\]
For a nearest \(Q\in\mathcal C_H\), choose \(Q_L\) as above.  The triangle inequality yields
\[
 d_{H,L}(R)
 \le\|R-Q_L\|_\infty
 \le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)+e_{H,L}.
\]
Rearranging and using nonnegativity proves the two distance bounds.

Enumerate the finite grid image as \(x^1,\ldots,x^G\).  Its coordinates are rational because grid weights are rational and all response indicators are zero or one.  For rational \(R\), \(d_{H,L}(R)\) is the value of the rational linear program
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 \text{minimize}&\delta\\
 \text{over}&\delta\ge0,\ \omega_g\ge0\\
 \text{subject to}&\displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^G\omega_g=1,\\
 &\displaystyle-\delta\le R_j-\sum_{g=1}^G\omega_gx^g_j\le\delta,
 \quad j=1,\ldots,m.
 \end{array}
\]
Its dual is
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 \text{maximize}&u^\top R-t\\
 \text{over}&u=u^+-u^-,\quad u^+,u^-\ge0,\quad t\in\mathbb R\\
 \text{subject to}&\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^m(u_j^++u_j^-)\le1,\\
 &t\ge u^\top x^g,\quad g=1,\ldots,G.
 \end{array}
\]
Indeed, every dual feasible point and every \(x=\sum_g\omega_gx^g\) satisfy
\[
 u^\top R-t\le u^\top(R-x)
 \le\|u\|_1\|R-x\|_\infty
 \le\|R-x\|_\infty,
\]
which is weak duality, while \(\texttt{lem:rational-linear-program-certificates}\) supplies equality of the finite optimal values and rational optimal basic solutions.  Exact substitution checks primal and dual feasibility.  Thus feasible rational certificates with objective gap at most any prescribed positive rational number give \(d^-\le d_{H,L}(R)\le d^+\).

Taking \(L_n=n\), \(\eta_n=1/n\), and \(R=\widehat P\), whose entries are integer multiples of \(1/n\), gives
\[
 d^-_{H,n}\le d_{H,L_n}(\widehat P),
 \qquad
 d^+_{H,n}-d^-_{H,n}\le\eta_n.
\]
The deterministic distance inequality then implies
\[
 \underline D_{H,n}
 =\max\{0,d^-_{H,n}-e_{H,L_n}\}
 \le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H).
\]
Finally,
\[
 e_{H,L}\le\frac{2(\min\{|H|,m\}-1)}{L}\longrightarrow0
\]
for fixed finite \(H\), and the primal--dual gap can be made arbitrarily small.  Choosing both errors below allocated portions of any requested positive tolerance yields a certified distance bracket of that precision.

For a path cell \(j=(a,b)\), let \(X_{ij}=\mathbf 1\{Y_{i1}=a,Y_{i2}=b\}\).  Under \(\texttt{ass:iid-consumers}\), these variables are iid Bernoulli with mean \(P_j\).  For a Bernoulli variable \(X\) with mean \(p\), direct differentiation of
\[
 \log\mathbb E\exp\{s(X-p)\}=-sp+\log(1-p+pe^s)
\]
shows that its second derivative is at most \(1/4\); the value and first derivative at zero vanish.  Two integrations therefore give
\[
 \log\mathbb E e^{s(X-p)}\le\frac{s^2}{8}.
\]
Markov's inequality applied to the product moment-generating function and minimization at \(s=4x\) yield
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat P_j-P_j\ge x\}\le e^{-2nx^2}.
\]
Applying the same calculation to \(-X\) gives the lower tail.  The union bound over the \(m\) cells and the definition
\[
 \rho_{n,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2m/\alpha)}{2n}}
\]
give
\[
 \Pr(E_n)\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 E_n:=\{\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
The bound contains no unknown distributional quantity, so it is uniform over the maintained model.

Let \(\kappa\in\Theta(P)\), and let \(H\) be the response set attached by \(\texttt{def:confidence-set}\) to its open price stratum or its breakpoint.  Then \(P\in\mathcal C_H\).  On \(E_n\),
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H)
 \le\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty
 \le\rho_{n,\alpha}.
\]
By \(\texttt{thm:certified-finite-menu-approximation}\), with the observable-moment-compressed \(e_{H,L_n}\),
\[
 \underline D_{H,n}
 \le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H)
 \le\rho_{n,\alpha}.
\]
Thus the construction retains the piece containing \(\kappa\).  If \(\kappa>K\), terminal equality gives \(H=F_\infty\), and the same argument applies to the separately tested terminal stratum.  Hence
\[
 E_n\subseteq\{\Theta(P)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\},
\]
which proves the asserted uniform whole-set coverage.  There is no multiplicity penalty over \(\kappa\): every conclusion holds on the same event \(E_n\).  By construction, retention of \((K,+\infty)\) makes the reported upper endpoint \(+\infty\).

For consistency of a finite declaration, set \(\delta=D_\infty(P)>0\).  The certificate gap gives
\[
 d^-_{F_\infty,n}
 \ge d_{\infty,L_n}(\widehat P)-\eta_n.
\]
Since \(\mathcal C_{\infty,L_n}\subseteq\mathcal C_\infty\), and since distance to a fixed closed set is one-Lipschitz,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \underline D_{F_\infty,n}
 &\ge d_{\infty,L_n}(\widehat P)-\eta_n-e_{F_\infty,L_n}\\
 &\ge\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_\infty)
       -\eta_n-e_{F_\infty,L_n}\\
 &\ge\delta-\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty
       -\eta_n-e_{F_\infty,L_n}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first inequality remains true when its right side is negative because \(\underline D_{F_\infty,n}\ge0\).  With \(L_n=n\),
\[
 e_{F_\infty,L_n}
 \le\frac{2(\min\{|F_\infty|,m\}-1)}{n}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \eta_n=\frac1n\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,\alpha}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The preceding exponential bound also implies \(\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty\to0\) in probability.  Therefore
\[
 \Pr\{\underline D_{F_\infty,n}>\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
With probability tending to one the terminal stratum is rejected; all remaining price pieces lie in \([0,K]\), so the reported upper endpoint is finite.  No uniform consistency statement is made at the boundary \(D_\infty(P)=0\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a nonempty finite response set \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\).  Define
\[
 T_H(q)=\bigl((r_a(q))_{a\in M_1},(s_{ab}(q))_{a\in M_1,b\in M_2}\bigr)
\]
and let \(d_H\) be the affine dimension of \(\operatorname{conv}T_H(\Delta(H))\).  Then \(d_H\le m-1\).  For every \(q\in\Delta(H)\), there is \(\bar q\in\Delta(H)\) supported on at most
\[
 \min\{|H|,d_H+1\}\le\min\{|H|,m\}
\]
response tables such that \(T_H(\bar q)=T_H(q)\).  In particular, \(v(\bar q)=v(q)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(I=|M_1|\) and \(B=|M_2|\), so \(m=IB\).  The map \(T_H\) is affine because every coordinate \(r_a\) and \(s_{ab}\) is linear in \(q\).  Consequently,
\[
 T_H(\Delta(H))
 =\operatorname{conv}\{T_H(e_f):f\in H\},
\]
where \(e_f\) is the unit mass on response table \(f\).  Every point in this convex hull satisfies
\[
 \sum_{a\in M_1}r_a=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{b\in M_2}s_{ab}=1\quad(a\in M_1).
\]
These are \(I+1\) independent affine equalities in the ambient space \(\mathbb R^{I+IB}\): the first involves only the \(r\)-coordinates, and each of the other \(I\) equalities involves a distinct block of \(s\)-coordinates.  Hence
\[
 d_H\le I+IB-(I+1)=IB-1=m-1.
\]

It remains to prove the support assertion without importing an additional theorem.  Express \(T_H(q)\) as a convex combination of the vertices \(T_H(e_f)\) carrying positive \(q_f\).  If more than \(d_H+1\) such vertices occur, their augmented vectors \((1,T_H(e_f))\) are linearly dependent in the \((d_H+1)\)-dimensional linear space generated by the affine hull.  Thus there are coefficients \(c_f\), not all zero, such that
\[
 \sum_f c_f=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_f c_fT_H(e_f)=0.
\]
After replacing \(c\) by \(-c\) if necessary, at least one \(c_f>0\).  Put
\[
 t=\min_{f:c_f>0}\frac{q_f}{c_f}>0,
 \qquad
 q_f^{\mathrm{new}}=q_f-tc_f.
\]
Then \(q^{\mathrm{new}}\ge0\), its coordinates sum to one, at least one formerly positive coordinate becomes zero, and
\[
 T_H(q^{\mathrm{new}})=T_H(q)-t\sum_fc_fT_H(e_f)=T_H(q).
\]
Repeating this finite elimination leaves at most \(d_H+1\) positive coordinates and never introduces support outside the original support, proving the bound by \(\min\{|H|,d_H+1\}\).  Finally, the definition \(v_{ab}=r_as_{ab}\) shows coordinate by coordinate that equality of \(T_H\) implies \(v(\bar q)=v(q)\).

added_lemmas.statement: For a finite-dimensional linear program in standard form with rational constraint matrix, rational right-hand side, and rational objective, if the primal is feasible and has a finite optimum then the primal and dual optimal values coincide and rational optimal basic feasible solutions exist.  Feasible rational primal and dual points whose objective values differ by at most a prescribed positive rational tolerance therefore certify lower and upper bounds with that gap.

added_lemmas.statement: A finite existential formula consisting of polynomial equalities and weak or strict polynomial inequalities with rational or represented real-algebraic coefficients is decidable by exact real-algebraic sign decomposition.  Real-algebraic inputs can be represented by defining integer polynomials and rational isolating intervals, and the output is certified by exact sign evaluations on the resulting cells.

source.locator: Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006), Chapters 2 and 14

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The constructed set \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) is finite, \(\mathcal C_\kappa=\mathcal C_\infty\) for every \(\kappa>K\), and, whenever \(\Theta(P)\ne\varnothing\), \(U(P)<+\infty\) if and only if \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\), equivalently if and only if \(D_\infty(P)>0\).  Moreover, \(\Theta(P)\) is relatively open in \([0,+\infty)\), is a finite union of intervals, and every finite upper endpoint lies in \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) and is not attained.  For arbitrary real \(P\), enumeration of the price strata gives a finite semialgebraic characterization of \(\Theta(P)\), and exact recovery of its upper endpoint is valid relative to an exact-real oracle that decides the displayed finite feasibility systems.  When the entries of \(P\) are rational or are supplied as represented real-algebraic numbers, rational root isolation and exact sign decomposition provide a certified implementation of those decisions.  No monotonicity of \(\kappa\mapsto\mathcal C_\kappa\) is presumed, and no unconditional finite algorithm is asserted for unrepresented arbitrary real inputs.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The observed table \(P\) may have arbitrary real entries.  Its finite membership systems are semialgebraic, but rational root isolation cannot unconditionally decide systems having unrepresented arbitrary-real coefficients.  The corrected claim preserves exact recovery relative to an exact-real feasibility oracle and gives an unconditional certified sign-decomposition implementation only for rational or represented real-algebraic input.

proposed.name: Dlower
proposed.def: For \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\), \(\underline D_{H,n}=\max\{0,d^-_{H,n}-e_{H,L_n}\}\), where \(e_{H,L_n}\) is the observable-moment-compressed deterministic grid error.
proposed.role: certified lower distance to the exact compatible body

proposed_core_edits.reason: The certified lower distance must explicitly inherit the observable-moment-compressed grid error.

proposed.name: Observable-moment-compressed rational-grid inner body and outer inflation
proposed.construction: For each finite-stratum response set \(F_\kappa\), form \(\mathcal G_{\kappa,L}\), set \(\mathcal C_{\kappa,L}=\operatorname{conv}v(\mathcal G_{\kappa,L})\), and inflate it by the observable-moment-compressed cube \([-e_{F_\kappa,L},e_{F_\kappa,L}]^m\).  Separately, form \(\mathcal G_{\infty,L}\) from \(F_\infty\), set \(\mathcal C_{\infty,L}=\operatorname{conv}v(\mathcal G_{\infty,L})\), and inflate it by \([-e_{F_\infty,L},e_{F_\infty,L}]^m\), where \(e_{H,L}=0\) for \(|H|=1\) and otherwise \(e_{H,L}=\min\{1,2(\min\{|H|,m\}-1)/L\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The outer inflation must use the improved observable-dimension error rather than the full response-set cardinality.

proposed.name: Certified whole-identified-set confidence region with observable-moment compression
proposed.construction: Set \(L_n=n\) and \(\eta_n=1/n\).  Compute the simultaneous box \(\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  For every finite open price stratum and every breakpoint value, use its own \(F_\kappa\) to compute rational primal and dual bounds \(d^-_{F_\kappa,n}\le d_{\kappa,L_n}(\widehat P)\le d^+_{F_\kappa,n}\) with gap at most \(\eta_n\), set \(\underline D_{F_\kappa,n}=\max\{0,d^-_{F_\kappa,n}-e_{F_\kappa,L_n}\}\) using the observable-moment-compressed grid error, and retain that parameter piece if and only if \(\underline D_{F_\kappa,n}\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  Separately use \(F_\infty\) to compute \(d^-_{F_\infty,n}\), set \(\underline D_{F_\infty,n}=\max\{0,d^-_{F_\infty,n}-e_{F_\infty,L_n}\}\), and retain the terminal stratum \((K,+\infty)\) if and only if \(\underline D_{F_\infty,n}\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  The union is \(\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Every finite-stratum and terminal retention test must subtract the revised observable-moment-compressed approximation error.

proposed.statement: For every finite design and every \(\kappa\ge0\), the set of path tables generated by the maintained model equals \(\mathcal C_\kappa=\operatorname{conv}\{v(q):q\in\Delta(F_\kappa)\}\). The body is compact, and every \(P\in\mathcal C_\kappa\) has an exact rationalization with at most \(m\) fixed-effect mixing types and conditionally iid absolutely continuous shocks supported inside strict response patches.
proposed.justification: This theorem converts an unrestricted latent distribution into an exact finite-dimensional curved probability body and proves constructive sharpness rather than only necessity.
proposed.gap: Mbakop establishes mixture-of-products geometry and nonpolyhedrality for conditional iid choice bodies, but does not derive the changing-menu switching-cost body or its upper-tail frontier.
proposed.consumer: Applied researchers can test exact compatibility of a turnover cell without specifying a parametric shock law or a distribution for plan fixed effects.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The revised proof invokes the load-bearing observable-moment compression lemma, so the dependency must be declared explicitly.

proposed.statement: The constructed set \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) is finite, \(\mathcal C_\kappa=\mathcal C_\infty\) for every \(\kappa>K\), and, whenever \(\Theta(P)\ne\varnothing\), \(U(P)<+\infty\) if and only if \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\), equivalently if and only if \(D_\infty(P)>0\).  Moreover, \(\Theta(P)\) is relatively open in \([0,+\infty)\), is a finite union of intervals, and every finite upper endpoint lies in \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) and is not attained.  For arbitrary real \(P\), enumeration of the price strata gives a finite semialgebraic characterization of \(\Theta(P)\), and exact recovery of its upper endpoint is valid relative to an exact-real oracle that decides the displayed finite feasibility systems.  When the entries of \(P\) are rational or are supplied as represented real-algebraic numbers, rational root isolation and exact sign decomposition provide a certified implementation of those decisions.  No monotonicity of \(\kappa\mapsto\mathcal C_\kappa\) is presumed, and no unconditional finite algorithm is asserted for unrepresented arbitrary real inputs.
proposed.justification: The theorem gives the observable necessary-and-sufficient condition for a finite switching-cost ceiling and reduces exact endpoint recovery to finitely many price regimes.
proposed.gap: Pakes et al. obtain common-menu moment-inequality bounds and state that their nonparametric changing-menu inequalities do not deliver an upper bound; neither they nor Mbakop characterize upper-tail saturation under turnover.
proposed.consumer: The health-choice application can retain year pairs crossing plan entry or exit precisely when the observed path table is separated from the terminal body.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed computational claim uses exact real-algebraic decision only under represented input and must declare that cited substrate together with the comparison and compatible-body definitions used directly in the proof.

proposed.statement: For every finite \(J\), every \(L\ge1\), and each \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\), \(\mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H\subseteq\mathcal C_{H,L}+[-e_{H,L},e_{H,L}]^m\).  Consequently, for every probability table \(R\), \(\max\{0,d_{H,L}(R)-e_{H,L}\}\le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)\le d_{H,L}(R)\).  For rational \(R\), the finite convex-hull program admits rational primal and dual certificates \(d^-\le d_{H,L}(R)\le d^+\) with any prescribed positive rational gap; in particular, \(L_n=n\) and \(\eta_n=1/n\) yield \(d^+-d^-\le\eta_n\) and \(\underline D_{H,n}=\max\{0,d^-_{H,n}-e_{H,L_n}\}\le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H)\).  Refinement reaches any requested strictly positive distance precision.
proposed.justification: The deterministic sandwich extends the exact small-design theory to any finite menu without presenting black-box optimization as analytic identification.
proposed.gap: Duarte et al. Theorem 1 on p. 7 proves sharpness of Algorithm 2's polynomial program, while Section 5 on pp. 8--10 and Algorithm 3 provide interruptible, progressively refined valid bounds and \(\varepsilon\)-sharpness. That general program does not give this conditional-iid quadratic-body grid sandwich, its closed deterministic error, or separate finite-stratum and terminal certificates; Kitamura--Stoye test a polyhedral random-utility cone.
proposed.consumer: Cells with more than three plans receive auditable included-point certificates, excluded-point separators, and a stopping rule at any positive tolerance.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem now depends directly on observable-moment compression, terminal nonemptiness, and rational linear-program duality certificates.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(U(P)<+\infty\iff D_\infty(P)=\operatorname{dist}_\infty(P,\mathcal C_\infty)>0\), with the exact finite value obtained by breakpoint-wise finite semialgebraic feasibility relative to an exact-real oracle; rational root-isolation and sign-decomposition certificates implement the search when \(P\) is rational or represented real algebraic.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline recovery guarantee must distinguish the mathematical semialgebraic characterization for arbitrary real \(P\) from implementable exact decisions for represented inputs.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The complete latent-free projection remains open for negative entry when both off-diagonal probabilities are positive, for zero-sign entry, and for all six exit classes, including every equality and zero-probability boundary and an explicit attaining mixture in each regime.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact negative-entry cone has eight coupled quadratic curve families sharing four square-coordinate budgets.  With both off-diagonal coordinates positive, its dual support function contains a switching term involving their minimum, so separately optimized face inequalities give only an outer description.  No frozen result eliminates these coupled allocations, and an unevaluated generic quantifier-elimination output is excluded by the target.
open_obligations.attempted: Strict-cycle tests enumerated all nine terminal classes; the binary-first-menu reduction enumerated all twenty two-patch curves; pure rays were removed; the negative and zero-sign entry cones were reduced to eight and seven nonredundant quadratic curve families; and the dual minimization over both off-diagonal coefficients was completed.  Positive-sign entry and two informative negative-sign faces were eliminated constructively.  The remaining route is the joint finite active-allocation case split, exact support comparison over all twenty curves, and the analogous three-first-choice allocation for exit.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Relabel the continuing plans \(a,b\), write
\[
 (A,B,C,R,S,T)=(P_{aa},P_{ab},P_{ac},P_{ba},P_{bb},P_{bc}),
\]
and put \(\tau=(p_{1a}-p_{1b})-(p_{2a}-p_{2b})\).  Exact strict-cycle enumeration gives the terminal entry response tables
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
&f_1=a&f_1=b\\ \hline
\tau<0&aaa,aab,aac,acc&bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc\\
\tau=0&aaa,aac,acc&bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc\\
\tau>0&aaa,aac,acc&baa,bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc.
\end{array}
\]
For exit, let \(L_0=bbb\), \(L_1=abb\), \(L_2=aba\), and \(L_3=aaa\).  The permitted indices for first choices \(a,b,c\), respectively, are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{initial status}&\operatorname{sign}(\tau)&a&b&c\\ \hline
b\text{ continues}&-&\{2,3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
b\text{ continues}&0&\{3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
b\text{ continues}&+&\{3\}&\{0,1,2,3\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&-&\{1,2,3\}&\{0,1\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&0&\{2,3\}&\{0,1\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&+&\{2,3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}.
\end{array}
\]
Each listed patch is open and nonempty by its strict comparisons.

For nonnegative \(a,c,s,h,b\), define
\[
 \Phi(a,c,s,h;b)=
 \bigl[bc\le h(a+c)\ \wedge\ b^2\le s(a+c)\bigr]
 \vee
 \bigl[bc>h(a+c)\ \wedge\ c(b-h)^2+ah^2\le sac\bigr].
\]
The complete constructive positive-entry formula is
\[
 P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 B\le R+T\ \wedge\ \Phi(A,C,S,T;B)
 \qquad(\tau>0).
\]
For negative entry, two complete boundary faces are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R=0:\quad&P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \Longleftrightarrow
 S\ge L\ \wedge\ \Phi(A,C,S-L,H;B),\\
 &L=\max\{0,B-T\},\qquad H=\min\{B,T\};\\[2mm]
 B=0:\quad&P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \Longleftrightarrow
 A\ge L\ \wedge\ R^2\le(A-L)(S+T),\\
 &L=\max\{0,R-C\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
These expressions expand into finite polynomial branches and include equality and zero boundaries with explicit rank-one allocations.

The full negative-entry cone is exactly generated by the four pure rays in coordinates \(A,C,S,T\) and the following eight curves, for \(s,t\ge0\):
\[
\begin{array}{l}
(s^2+st,0,0,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2+st,0,0,st,0,t^2),\\
(s^2,st,0,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2,0,st,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2,0,st,st,0,t^2),\\
(s^2,st,0,0,t^2+st,0),\\
(s^2,st,0,0,t^2,st),\\
(0,st,s^2,0,t^2,st).
\end{array}
\]
The zero-sign cone removes the sixth curve.  If \(a,c,s,t\ge0\) are dual coefficients on the pure-ray coordinates and \(b,r\) are the coefficients on \(B,R\), exact nonnegativity on these curves is equivalent to
\[
 r\ge-\rho,
 \qquad b\ge-\beta,
 \qquad b+r\ge-\gamma,
\]
where
\[
 \rho=\min(a,c)+2\sqrt{a\min(s,t)},
 \qquad
 \beta=\min\{s+2\sqrt{as},t+2\sqrt{as},t+2\sqrt{cs}\},
 \qquad
 \gamma=2\sqrt{as}.
\]
For fixed \(a,c,s,t\), minimizing over \(b,r\) gives
\[
 -\left[B\beta+R\rho-\min(B,R)\max\{\beta+\rho-\gamma,0\}\right].
\]
The coupled term is the exact obstruction to obtaining the positive-off-diagonal negative-entry body by intersecting the two solved faces.

prose_updates.tldr: Plan persistence confounds switching costs with stable consumer-by-plan tastes, while existing nonparametric health-choice bounds discard year pairs with plan entry or exit.  The project maps each turnover cell to strict utility-comparison graphs and the convex hull of a conditional-iid quadratic probability map, proves terminal saturation after finitely many rational price breakpoints, and characterizes a finite ceiling by positive distance from the terminal body.  Exact breakpoint recovery is a finite semialgebraic problem, interpreted relative to an exact-real oracle for arbitrary real \(P\) and implemented by certified sign decomposition for rational or represented real-algebraic input.  Observable-moment compression yields a finite-menu grid error depending on \(\min\{|H|,m\}\).  The positive-sign three-plan entry class and two negative-sign boundary faces have constructive formulas; the complete latent-free Boolean elimination remains explicitly open in \(\texttt{oeq:three-plan-analytic-body}\).

project_justification.gap: Pakes et al. Condition 2.2 and Theorem 2.3(a), PDF p. 20 of the canonical revised-July-2025 manuscript, require the two comparator subsets to coincide in a common choice universe and deliver the resulting joint probability inequality. Entry or exit changes the feasible winner--loser comparisons and prevents that common-universe samplewise containment from covering the full observed menus. Mbakop's conditional-iid geometry shows that adding more linear inequalities cannot generally recover sharpness. No inspected paper gives an exact upper-tail saturation theorem, an observable finite-ceiling criterion, or a complete analytic three-plan turnover body.
project_justification.niche: Two observed post-initial choices are short enough that conditional iid becomes a quadratic mixture-of-products restriction, yet menu turnover makes this curved geometry economically consequential rather than a generic computation exercise.
project_justification.fill: The project derives finite terminal comparison graphs, expresses each exact compatible body as the convex hull of a quadratic map, proves the observable finite-ceiling equivalence, and gives finite semialgebraic breakpoint feasibility with exact-real and represented-input qualifications.  It supplies constructive formulas for positive-sign three-plan entry and two negative-sign boundary faces, while retaining the remaining three-plan latent-free Boolean elimination as \(\texttt{oeq:three-plan-analytic-body}\).  Observable-moment compression, certified grid inflation, and simultaneous multinomial inversion extend the proved kernel to arbitrary finite menus.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the \(m\)-cell path law \(P\) is estimated, by multinomial frequencies \(\widehat P\); latent laws are profiled out by exact compatibility.  Observable-moment compression gives \(e_{H,L}=\min\{1,2(\min\{|H|,m\}-1)/L\}\) for non-singleton \(H\).  Inference fixes \(L_n=n\) and \(\eta_n=1/n\), uses rational primal--dual distance certificates because \(\widehat P\) is rational, and tests the terminal response set separately from every finite price stratum and breakpoint.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The proposal treats one known two-choice design cell with stable plan quality, a common \(\kappa\), unrestricted fixed-effect mixing, and the fixed-cell sequential-exogeneity and stationarity factorization encoded by conditionally iid shocks.  Its maintained class is the published Pakes et al. fixed-cell class intersected with explicit unique-choice and conditional full-vector Lebesgue absolute-continuity regularity, not the whole published class.  Necessity uses the factorization and no ties; sufficiency uses the stronger absolutely continuous conditional-iid construction.  If \(P\in\mathcal C_\infty\), unboundedness constructed in this subclass transfers to every larger class by inclusion; if \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\), exclusion from the subclass does not by itself exclude the larger class.  The proposal does not identify welfare, validate cells whose plan quality changes, impose monotonicity of \(\Theta(P)\), promise an exact finite algorithm for unrepresented arbitrary-real \(P\), or claim uniform consistency when \(D_\infty(P)=0\).  Complete latent-free elimination beyond the proved three-plan entry regimes remains \(\texttt{oeq:three-plan-analytic-body}\).  An SSRN record reports an April 2026 revision of Pakes et al., but its manuscript was inaccessible during the bounded search; comparison against that text remains a presolve condition if it becomes available.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem converts the stated fixed-cell conditional factorization into a convex hull of a quadratic path map and supplies an exact conditionally iid, absolutely continuous construction for the reverse inclusion; it does not silently extend the equality to a larger published class.

The theorem gives the observable finite-ceiling criterion and finitely many price regimes.  For arbitrary real \(P\), exact recovery is relative to an exact-real feasibility oracle; rational or represented real-algebraic tables admit certified sign decomposition.  Constructive unboundedness transfers upward by subclass inclusion, whereas subclass exclusion does not.

Compression of the observable moment vector before rational rounding replaces response-set-size inflation by the certified radius based on \(\min\{|H|,m\}\), making the deterministic guarantee depend on observable dimension.

One simultaneous multinomial event covers the entire identified set, and the revised lower distance propagates the observable-moment-compressed numerical error without a multiplicity penalty over switching-cost values.

Constructive formulas are proved for positive-sign entry and two negative-sign boundary faces, but the joint positive-off-diagonal allocation, zero-sign entry, and exit eliminations remain open and are not represented as a completed theorem.
